SMTO-SKL-0029 — Google Calendar didn't send back a usable answer

GUID: d978706e-0a88-5ecb-9248-6317fa1f6bd7
Slug: google-calendar-provider-unavailable
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-calendar

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't get a reliable answer from Google Calendar. The connection may have dropped, or Google sent back something unexpected. This step didn't change your calendar.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the computer running SMTO is connected to the internet, for example by opening a website on it. SMTO needs internet access to reach Google Calendar.
  2. Open Google Calendar in your browser to check it's working. If Google Calendar is having trouble, SMTO can't get answers from it either.
  3. Wait a few minutes, then ask SMTO for the calendar task again. Short network or Google problems usually clear up, and this step didn't change anything, so asking again is safe.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows your calendar information or completes the change without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. If an earlier step reported it couldn't confirm a change, check Google Calendar for that change before asking for it again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Google Calendar read failed after bounded retries (network error, timeout, oversized body or 5xx), or returned a malformed list, cursor or mismatched calendar or event ID; any pending write was not sent.

What this means

  • Calendar reads encounter server/transport failures, malformed collections or mismatched returned resource identities; pre-write reads can fail the same checks. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Calendar reads encounter server/transport failures, malformed collections or mismatched returned resource identities; pre-write reads can fail the same checks.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect status, exception, response shape and expected identity rather than assuming a Google outage.

How to fix it

  • Check the Server's network access to www.googleapis.com and Google Workspace status, then request another read. If the failure was a malformed or mismatched response, read the exact calendar or event again; reconcile any separate uncertain write before repeating it.
  • Check the recorded transport or response-validation failure, restore a usable read, and reconcile any uncertain write before repeating it.

Retry and execution caution

  • Check Google availability and network connectivity, then request another read. Uncertain writes require reconciliation before another mutation.

How to verify the fix

  • A bounded read returns a valid same-resource response; uncertain writes remain separately reconciled.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials or private Calendar content in diagnostics.
  • Do not blindly repeat writes after uncertain provider effects.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
